description: Fig. 6 is a five-panel composite of optical micrographs (OM) of transverse cross-sections of SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni low-density steel, one panel per laser power. Each panel shows a featureless light beige (as-polished) matrix carrying dark, irregularly shaped pores, and every panel has a 500 µm scale bar in its lower-right corner. (a) P-70 is annotated "Porosity=4.75 %" and is by far the most defective: a dense field of dark angular pores of varying size plus one bright white angular particle near the left-centre. (b) P-90, "Porosity=0.25 %", shows only sparse small dark specks. (c) P-110, "Porosity=0.13 %", is almost free of resolvable porosity, with a handful of tiny dark dots. The fourth panel carries no printed panel letter or porosity value in the supplied image; it shows very few small dark defects and one slightly elongated dark feature near the centre — the caption assigns this panel to (d) P-130 with porosity 0.28 %. (e) P-150, "Porosity=0.35 %", shows again more dark defects, several elongated and needle-like, one explicitly labelled "Crack" with an arrow. The figure demonstrates that porosity is minimised at intermediate laser power (P-110) and rises at both the lowest (P-70) and the highest (P-150) powers. No numeric axis values are printed.

observations.observation: Each of the five panels carries a 500 µm scale bar in its lower-right corner, confirming all micrographs are at the same magnification.
Panel (a) contains a much higher density of dark, irregularly shaped pores than panels (b)-(e), including several large angular pores.
Panel (a) contains a single bright white angular particle (unmelted powder or inclusion) near the left-centre of the field of view.
Printed annotations on the panels read exactly "Porosity=4.75 %" (a), "Porosity=0.25 %" (b), "Porosity=0.13 %" (c) and "Porosity=0.35 %" (e).
Panel (e) has the word "Crack" with an arrow pointing to an elongated, needle-like dark defect at the left of the field of view.
Panel (c) appears nearly featureless, with the lowest resolvable pore density of the five panels.
The fourth micrograph in the group shows no printed panel letter or porosity value; the caption assigns it to (d) with "Porosity=0.28 %".
The caption states Fig. 6 shows OM images of transverse cross-sections of SLM-printed Fe–30Mn–9Al–C–3Ni alloys: (a) P-70, (b) P-90, (c) P-110, (d) P-130, and (e) P-150.
The citing text states the P-70, P-90, P-110, P-130 and P-150 samples were determined to be 4.75%, 0.25%, 0.13%, 0.28% and 0.35% porous, respectively.
The citing text states that porosity first decreases and then increases with increasing laser power.
The citing text states relative density first increased and then decreased with increasing laser power.
